results.title: A controlled study of remote software development output
results.content: In a 2023 controlled study, remote developers committed 8% more code per week than their in-office peers, though the authors caution that commit volume is a weak proxy for value delivered.

results.title: Developer Survey 2024: working arrangements
results.content: Self-reported productivity rose for 62% of surveyed remote developers, while 21% reported a decline concentrated among engineers with under two years of experience.

results.title: Effects of remote work on collaboration networks
results.content: Telemetry covering 61,000 employees showed collaboration networks became more siloed after the shift to remote work, with fewer bridging ties between teams.

results.title: Code review latency in distributed teams
results.content: Median code review turnaround increased from 6 hours to 11 hours in distributed teams, with the largest increases spanning time zones more than four hours apart.

results.title: Follow-up: review latency and team distribution
results.content: A follow-up analysis confirmed the 6-to-11-hour median shift and attributed roughly half of the increase to reviewer availability windows rather than reviewer effort.

results.title: Meta-analysis of remote work productivity findings
results.content: Across 14 studies the pooled effect on productivity was small and not statistically distinguishable from zero, and heterogeneity between studies was high.

results.title: Onboarding outcomes for remote engineering hires
results.content: Remote hires reached their first independent production change 3 weeks later on average than in-office hires at the same companies.
